content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (anilide). The amide is attached to the α,β-unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the amide carbonyl is part of the chain. So step 1: disconnect amide to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the acid) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide precursor: the acid is the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring? Wait the acid would be the same chain but with COOH instead of CONH-aryl. So product after step 1: α,β-unsaturated acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Actually the sulfonamide part is separate: The sulfonamide attaches to the first phenyl ring (para-methyl phenyl). So the target has sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings: first phenyl with methyl and sulfonamide to second phenyl which has the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus step 1: amide formation: break C(=O)N bond to give α,β-unsaturated acid (with same phenyl-sulfonamide attached) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (the acid). Precursor B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2: Doebner modification: the α,β-unsaturated acid is formed from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with sulfonamide) reacting with malonic acid. So break the C=C bond and the carboxylate to give aldehyde and malonic acid. The aldehyde precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (i.e., the phenyl-sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing aldehyde). The other precursor: malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Good.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: break the S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl ring and an amine (the first phenyl ring with methyl). So precursor: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) Cc1ccc(N)cc1 and sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-c2ccc(...?) Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring (the one bearing aldehyde). So sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (the aromatic sulfonyl chloride). So step 3: combine p-toluidine with that sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with nested reactions.

Root molecule: target SMILES.

Children: reaction node (step 1) with template_id (we need to find appropriate template). We can search for amide formation template (functional groups broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide). We already got template list earlier: reaction_id 401931 etc. That template seems to be amide formation from acid and amine? The canonical smarts: C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5] . This seems to be coupling of acid (with alkene) to amine to form amide. So we can use template_id 401931.

Step 2: Doebner modification template. Need to find template that forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. Search for functional groups broken: aldehydes, carboxylic acids? Actually forward reaction: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid + CO2. So broken: aldehyde, carboxylic acid (one of the two). Formed: C-C double bond. Let's search.
